messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered: Auth Service — unusually high rate of JWT validation failures detected (5000/min threshold). Paging on-call and escalation policy alpha.
pagerduty: PD-INC-4521 created, priority: P1. Notifying: Ayesha (oncall), Policy: Auth-SRE-Escalate. Initial trigger: 2026-03-14T09:17:09Z.
Ayesha (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. — quick triage: what endpoints/customers affected?
Kai (support): seeing ~15 open customer tickets referencing 401s on API requests to /v1/connect since 09:16 UTC. Sample clients: acct-A123, acct-B234, integration: stripe-webhooks. Screenshot pasted in support thread.
Miguel (auth): I have logs — large spike of InvalidSignature errors. Payloads show token kid="test-local-001" and alg=RS256. That kid shouldn't exist in prod JWKS. Looks like some tokens being signed by a local fallback keystore.
Miguel (auth): excerpt from auth-validate.log: ```
2026-03-14T09:16:58Z ERROR validate_token req_id=xyz InvalidSignature kid=test-local-001
2026-03-14T09:16:59Z WARN  jwks_fetch service=auth JWKS cache hit=false url=https://auth.redwood/api/.well-known/jwks.json
2026-03-14T09:17:01Z INFO  signer selected=local-keystore fallback=true instance=auth-pod-7f9b
```
Jules (infra): I just checked deployments. We rolled a small canary yesterday that enabled ENABLE_LOCAL_KEY=true on the canary pool to test HSM cold-start regressions. Looks like one canary pod got scheduled into the prod pool in us-west-2 due to label mismatch. That pod is signing tokens with the test key that was seeded on image build.
Ayesha (oncall): Ok plan proposal: 1) remove the canary env/label so no more local keys get used 2) force restart affected pods in us-west-2 3) purge any cached local keystores 4) if necessary re-issue tokens for internal services and inform external customers. Who can do 1-3 now?
Jules (infra): I'm on step 1 and 2. Running:
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/auth-service ENABLE_LOCAL_KEY=false --record
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/auth-service -l region=us-west-2
```
Jules (infra): kicked that off 09:19 UTC. Rolling restart across 4 pods, throttled 1 at a time.
Elena (sre): I'll monitor error rates, latency, and 5xx/401 counts. Setting alert: if 401s don't drop 50% in 10m, escalate to oncall lead.
Miguel (auth): In parallel I'm going to purge the local keystore on any pod that reported fallback=true. Command to run (on each node):
```
ssh auth-node-XX sudo rm -f /var/local/auth_keystore/* && systemctl restart auth-service
```
Kai (support): FYI customers on the support queue that reported failures are mostly on us-west endpoints. They're asking for ETA. Suggested message: "We're investigating a token validation issue impacting some requests in US-West; no data exposure; mitigation in progress. Will update in 15 minutes."
Ayesha (oncall): Good. Send that. Also create a short status note for PagerDuty incident and add affected customer tags.
pagerduty: Incident PD-INC-4521 acknowledged by Ayesha (oncall) at 2026-03-14T09:19:35Z. Escalation timer paused.
Jules (infra): Restart completed for pod auth-pod-7f9b at 09:22 UTC. Confirmed it no longer presents the local key on startup. I also removed the canary label mapping that caused scheduling leak.
Miguel (auth): Rechecked logs — tokens signed with kid=test-local-001 dropped to 0 after 09:23 UTC. Validation error rate down 92%.
Elena (sre): Metrics: 401s on /v1/connect in us-west down from 320/min to 18/min in 4 minutes. System health: ok. I'll keep monitoring for another 10 minutes.
Ayesha (oncall): Any lingering customers who need token re-issuance? Miguel, can you list affected internal service-client tokens we should rotate proactively?
Miguel (auth): Internal list small: service-webhook-consumer, integration-proxy. I'll issue short-lived fallback tokens and invalidate the ones with kid=test-local-001. Rotation script run at 09:30 UTC.
Kai (support): Sending status update to affected customers now. Included steps we took and expected ETA ~15m. No PII exposure, just auth failures.
Elena (sre): Observability check: no increase in error budget burn and no other regions impacted. Canary logic review ticket created: GH-3912 (assign Jules + Miguel).
Ayesha (oncall): Good job. Next: postmortem template please — assign owners and timeline. I'll keep incident open until we confirm no residual errors for 30m.
Miguel (auth): Root cause hypothesis: the canary rollout allowed a pod with ENABLE_LOCAL_KEY=true into prod due to a label selector bug; that pod had a build-time seeded test keystore. The signing tier should never fall back to a local key in prod — we need a hard guard in code and a stricter admission check.
Jules (infra): Action items: 1) revert canary config and patch deployment selectors (done) 2) add admission controller rule to prevent pods with env ENABLE_LOCAL_KEY=true from scheduling in prod 3) add unit test to CI to ensure no test keystore in prod images.
Ayesha (oncall): PagerDuty, please escalate to SRE lead if this regresses within 72 hours.
pagerduty: Escalation rule registered; incident will auto-escalate if a similar alert triggers within 72h.
Elena (sre): Monitoring window clear at 09:48 UTC — error rates stable and support queues not increasing. I'll mark metrics stable and start drafting postmortem notes.
Ayesha (oncall): Marking incident as resolved in PD. Thanks everyone for quick responses. Follow-ups: GH-3912 (config), GH-3913 (admission rule), GH-3914 (postmortem).
incident-bot: Incident PD-INC-4521 resolved by Ayesha (oncall) at 2026-03-14T09:48:30Z. Auto-close in 60 minutes. Reaction: :white_check_mark:
